text: An annotation is declared, read reflectively, and never found. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The annotated members are private, and annotations are readable only on public ones.
Its retention is not `RUNTIME`, so it did not survive into the loaded class.
It lacks a member named `value`, which reflection requires in order to match.
`@Target` was omitted, so the compiler discarded it as unplaceable.
explanation: The default retention is `CLASS` — kept in the class file but not loaded — which is almost never what anyone wants. It is the commonest annotation bug precisely because everything compiles and there is no error to read; the code simply finds nothing. Chapter 27 gives the three retention policies and the four kinds of reader.
